stakeholders.name: Smallholder Farmer Community
stakeholders.description: ~85 million smallholder farming households across Punjab, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh depend on input pricing, water access, and market linkages. They have high political power through farmer unions and cooperative networks.

engagement_tactics.option: Co-invest in farmer training and soil health programs
engagement_tactics.rationale: Builds long-term social licence, aligns with SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), reduces input cost volatility
Creates land displacement and social conflict

engagement_tactics.option: Issue annual CSR report on farmer welfare
engagement_tactics.rationale: Reporting without action does not build trust

stakeholders.name: State Groundwater Boards
stakeholders.description: Regulatory bodies with authority to issue extraction limits, impose penalties, and revoke agricultural licences in water-stressed districts across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Tamil Nadu.

engagement_tactics.option: Implement drip irrigation and water recycling across operations
Commission third-party water audits and share results proactively
engagement_tactics.rationale: Builds credibility and pre-empts enforcement actions

stakeholders.name: SEBI / BRSR Reporting Authority
stakeholders.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India mandates BRSR (Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report) compliance for top listed companies. Non-compliance triggers penalties and analyst downgrades.

engagement_tactics.option: File comprehensive BRSR with all 9 NGRBC principles
engagement_tactics.rationale: Demonstrates full compliance and ESG leadership
Meets baseline but signals low ESG ambition to investors

stakeholders.name: Agri-Environmental NGOs
stakeholders.description: Civil society organisations including Navdanya, IFOAM South Asia, and WWF-India monitor agrochemical use, biodiversity loss, and farmer welfare. They have strong media relationships and can escalate campaigns.

engagement_tactics.option: Partner with NGOs on regenerative agriculture pilots
engagement_tactics.rationale: Converts critics into co-investors in your ESG narrative

engagement_tactics.option: Deny NGO access to farm sites for audits
engagement_tactics.rationale: Triggers adversarial campaigns and reputational damage

stakeholders.name: ESG-Mandated Institutional Investors
stakeholders.description: FIIs and domestic mutual funds with ESG mandates (including SBI Mutual Fund ESG funds and global LPs like Norges Bank) evaluate water risk, governance quality, and BRSR compliance in allocation decisions.

engagement_tactics.option: Publish TCFD-aligned climate risk report annually
Focus investor relations on earnings only
engagement_tactics.rationale: Ignores the ESG screening criteria used by major funds

stakeholders.name: Rural Village Panchayats
stakeholders.description: Village-level governance bodies hold social licence to operate in rural areas. They can block land access, organise labour actions, and escalate to district collectors if operations harm local livelihoods.

engagement_tactics.option: Establish community advisory boards and rural livelihood funds
engagement_tactics.rationale: Builds structural SLO at the community level

engagement_tactics.option: Offer one-time cash payments in lieu of ongoing engagement
engagement_tactics.rationale: Transactional approach does not build durable SLO
